copy_text: Home Privacy Policy [ Legal ] Privacy Policy How Reinforce Lab collects, uses and protects your information when you use our website, forms and store, and the choices you have. Last updated: 7 October 2026 On this page Who we are What this policy covers What we collect Cookies Orders and payments How we use your information Who we share it with International transfers How long we keep it How we protect it Your rights Children Links to other websites Changes to this policy Contact us Who we are Reinforce Lab Limited (registered in Bangladesh, RJSC registration no. C-180618/2022) is the company responsible for your information (the “data controller”). Our registered office is Suite #1402, Level-13, Concord Tower, 113 Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, Dhaka 1000, Bangladesh. We also work from 2511 Pines Pointe Dr, Katy, TX 77493, USA, through our US company, Reinforce Lab Inc. For anything about privacy, email hello@reinforcelab.com . We have not appointed a data protection officer; your email reaches the people who handle these requests. What this policy covers This policy covers our website, our forms, our online store and the emails you send us. When you become a client, the information we handle for you (for example access to your analytics or your website) is covered by our agreement with you. What we collect Information you give us Contact form: your name and email address, and, if you choose, your company, website, the topic and your message. Search Authority Diagnostic and SEO & AI Search Audit request form: your name, work email and company, and, if you choose, your website, role, industry, biggest search challenge, monthly content volume and desired outcome. Orders from our store: see “Orders and payments” below. Emails and calls: whatever you choose to tell us when you email or phone us. Fields marked as required are the minimum we need to reply to you; everything else is optional. Each form tells you, before you send it, why we need your details, how long we keep them, where they are stored and how to withdraw, and asks you to tick a box to agree. We record that you agreed and when. Please do not send us sensitive information, such as health information, through the forms. Information collected automatically Website analytics: if you agree to analytics cookies, we use Google Analytics to understand how the website is used. See “Cookies” below. Visit statistics: we use Jetpack Stats, a service from Automattic, to count visits and see which pages are read. Your browser connects to Automattic’s servers, which receive technical information such as your IP address, browser type and the pages you view. We see totals, not who you are. Jetpack Stats does not set cookies on our pages. Fonts: our fonts are served from our own website, not from Google, so loading a page does not send your information to a font provider. Spam protection: when you send a form, we keep a scrambled (hashed) version of your IP address for one hour to limit repeated submissions. It is then deleted automatically. Server logs: our hosting provider, Hostinger, records technical requests (IP address, date and time, page requested) to keep the website running and secure. Cookies Cookies are small files a website stores in your browser. We use two kinds: Cookie What it does When it is set How long it lasts Google Analytics ( _ga , _ga_* ) Tells visits apart so we can see how the website is used, in totals Only after you accept analytics cookies Up to 2 years Your cookie choice ( rl_consent , kept in your browser’s local storage, not a cookie) Remembers whether you accepted or declined analytics cookies, so we do not ask on every page When you choose 6 months, then we ask again Store and login cookies (WooCommerce, WordPress) Keep your cart and checkout working, and keep our team logged in When you use the cart or checkout, or log in From the end of your visit up to a few days When you first visit, we ask whether you accept analytics cookies. If you decline, or your browser sends a Global Privacy Control signal, no analytics cookies are set and the website works the same. You can change your choice at any time with the “Cookie settings” link at the bottom of every page, or by clearing cookies in your browser. Orders and payments When you buy from our store, we collect what we need to process and deliver your order: your name, email address, phone number, billing address, the products you buy and your order history. Payments are made through our payment provider: you enter your card or payment details on the provider’s secure form, the provider processes the payment, and we do not see or store your full card number. We will name our payment provider on this page before the store opens on this website. We use order information to complete your order, send receipts and updates, handle refunds and support, and keep the records that tax and accounting laws require. How we use your information What we do Why we are allowed to Reply to your message or request Your consent, given with the tick box on the form; you asked us to (steps before a possible contract); and our legitimate interest in answering enquiries Prepare your Search Authority Diagnostic or audit proposal Your consent, given on the form, and steps you asked us to take before a possible contract Follow up about your request Our legitimate interest in following up an enquiry you made; you can tell us to stop at any time Process and deliver store orders, and handle refunds Our contract with you Measure how the website is used with Google Analytics Your consent, which you can withdraw at any time Keep the website working, secure and free of spam Our legitimate interest in running a safe website Count visits in totals with Jetpack Stats Our legitimate interest in improving the website Keep tax and accounting records for orders and clients Legal obligation We do not sell your information. We do not use it for advertising, and we do not add you to a newsletter unless you ask to join one. We do not make decisions about you based only on automated processing. Who we share it with We share only what each provider needs to do its job for us: Hostinger, which hosts our website and our email, including the hello@reinforcelab.com mailbox that receives form messages; Google (Google Analytics, only with your consent) and Automattic (Jetpack Stats), as described above; our payment provider, for store orders; professional advisers, such as accountants or lawyers, when needed; authorities, when the law requires it. International transfers Reinforce Lab Limited is based in Bangladesh, and our team also works from the United States. When you send us a form or an email, you send your information directly to us. Our service providers may process it in other countries; when they do, we rely on their safeguards, such as the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses where they apply, and we transfer information out of Bangladesh only as Bangladesh’s data protection law allows. How long we keep it Form submissions and emails that do not lead to work: up to 24 months, then deleted. Information about clients and store orders: for as long as we work together or the order needs support, then as long as tax and accounting laws require. Google Analytics data: up to 14 months. Spam-protection records: one hour. How we protect it The website uses HTTPS. Form submissions are stored as private records that only our team can open, and access is limited to the people who need it. No method of sending or storing information is completely secure, but we work to protect yours and will tell you and the authorities about a serious breach as quickly as the law requires (for example within 72 hours to the authority under the GDPR). Your rights Depending on where you live, you can ask us to: tell you what information we hold about you and give you a copy; correct it; delete it; stop or limit how we use it, or object to a use based on our legitimate interests; send it to you or another company in a common format; withdraw consent you gave, at any time, without affecting what we did before. To make a request, email hello@reinforcelab.com . We will reply within one month and may ask you to confirm who you are. Depending on where you live European Union and European Economic Area: you have the rights above under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and you can complain to the data protection authority in your country. United Kingdom: you have the same rights under the UK GDPR and can complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office. Bangladesh: under the Personal Data Protection Ordinance 2025, your personal data belongs to you. We process it with your consent or where the law allows without it, you can withdraw consent at any time and we then stop that processing, and you can ask to see, correct or delete your data. United States: you can ask what we collect and ask us to delete it. We do not sell personal information or share it for targeted advertising. If your browser sends a Global Privacy Control signal, we treat it as a request to opt out and do not load analytics cookies. Elsewhere: we give everyone the rights above, whatever the local law requires. Children Our website, store and services are for adults and businesses. We do not knowingly collect information from anyone under 18, and we never track or profile children or show them targeted advertising. If you think a child has sent us information, email us and we will delete it. Links to other websites Our pages link to other websites, such as LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, Clutch and the sources we cite. Their own privacy policies apply when you visit them. Changes to this policy When we change this policy we update the date at the top of this page. If a change is significant, we will say so here. SEO data sits in one tool. Content research happens somewhere else. Writers don't know what customers are complaining about. Nobody is connecting the signals, and more content isn't the answer. You rank on Google but vanish in AI search. ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overviews now answer what your pages used to. You find out from a prospect, weeks late. Your content can't prove what it claims. In regulated industries, an unsupported statement isn't a nuisance; it's a liability. AI writes an article in 30 seconds. That's not the problem. Thin, unverified, undifferentiated content that Google stops indexing. That's the problem. You measure output, not authority. Word counts and publish cadence tell you nothing about whether you're actually winning the search. Rankings slip and no one knows why. SERP shifted? Intent changed? Content decayed? Cannibalization? By the time you diagnose it, the traffic is gone. Every tool is a silo. Five subscriptions, three teams, zero feedback loops. You are the integration layer, and it doesn't scale. Four disciplines get mixed up. They overlap, but each has its own goal. AI Search Optimization is the umbrella for being visible in AI search; GEO and LLM Optimization are specialist layers inside it. You will also see it sold as AI SEO, AI optimization (AIO), answer engine optimization (AEO) or AI-powered search engine optimization: different names for the same goal. Ranking on Google does not mean an AI will name you. These are the usual reasons, and what we do about each. 01 · Access AI crawlers can't read you Robots rules, firewalls or script-only pages stop AI crawlers from reaching the content you want quoted. Fix Crawler policy, llms.txt and server-rendered pages. 02 · Entity The AI isn't sure who you are Different names, descriptions and profiles across the web make your brand hard to identify, or easy to confuse. Fix One consistent entity, schema and linked profiles. 03 · Content Nothing clean to quote Long pages that never answer the question directly give AI engines nothing to lift. Fix Answer-first pages built around real buyer questions. 04 · Evidence Claims without sources Unsupported claims are risky to repeat, especially in health, pharma and finance. Fix Every important claim tied to a source and checked by a person. 05 · Authority No one else vouches for you AI engines lean on independent sources. If trusted third parties never mention you, a competitor gets named instead. Fix Earned mentions, reviews, digital PR and link building. 06 · Measurement No one is checking Most teams don't know which prompts mention them, or whether the description is even right. Fix A tracked prompt set, engine by engine. Sources: Google Search Central: Robots.txt introduction · Google: common crawlers, including Google-Extended · OpenAI: crawlers and user agents · Perplexity: crawlers [ How it works ] How does AI Search Optimization work? Five steps, run as a loop. Measurement comes first, so every fix is judged against a baseline. 01 Baseline Build a prompt set from real buyer questions and search intent (search queries, sales and customer questions) and record where you are mentioned, cited and described, against named competitors. 02 Open access Check that AI crawlers can reach the right pages, agree your crawler policy, publish an llms.txt and make sure content is in the page's HTML. 03 Clarify the entity One name, one description, structured data and linked profiles, so every engine knows who you are, what you do and who you serve. 04 Content & evidence Answer-first pages and question-led headings, with every important claim sourced and reviewed before it ships. 05 Authority & monitoring Earn the third-party mentions AI engines trust, re-run the prompt set, and correct anything the engines get wrong. Sources: llms.txt proposal (llmstxt.org) · Google Search Central: Intro to structured data · Google Search Central: AI features and your website · Aggarwal et al., GEO: Generative Engine Optimization (arXiv, 2023) Step 1 is free. The Search Authority Diagnostic is your baseline: where you stand in Google and in AI answers today, and what to fix first. AI-access fixes : crawler policy, llms.txt and rendering checks. Entity & schema plan : Organization, Service and FAQ markup and consistent profiles. Content roadmap : the pages to create, rewrite or refresh first, grouped by topic to build topical authority. Accuracy review : where AI tools describe you wrongly, and the sources behind it. Monthly reporting : mentions, citations, accuracy and AI referral traffic, with next actions. From $5,000 setup AI search optimization is part of every Search Authority OS package, from $5,000 setup plus $1,500 to $2,500 a month. Not ready to commit? Start with the free diagnostic. Get your free diagnostic → See the packages → [ Measurement ] How do we measure AI visibility? Rankings alone can't show AI visibility. We report five measures, per engine, on your prompt set. Mention rate How often your brand is named in answers to your prompts. Citation rate How often your pages are linked as a source. A generative engine doesn't hand out a list of ten links. It searches, reads, picks passages and writes an answer, citing the sources it relied on. The question expands Engines often break one question into several related searches. Google calls this "query fan-out" in AI Mode. Pages are retrieved The engine pulls candidate pages it can crawl and trusts for each of those searches. Passages are extracted It reads passages, not whole pages, and keeps the ones that answer clearly and specifically. The answer is written and cited The chosen passages are combined into one answer, with links to the pages they came from. What the research says The term GEO comes from a peer-reviewed study by researchers at Princeton University and IIT Delhi, presented at ACM KDD 2024. Testing content changes across a benchmark of diverse queries, they found that GEO methods could boost a source's visibility in generative engine responses by up to 40%, and that the best method varies by domain. Adding citations to credible sources, quotations and statistics were among the strongest methods; keyword stuffing was not. Source: Aggarwal et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024. arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735 [ Example ] What does a citable passage look like? The same idea, written two ways. What is Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)? Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is the practice of structuring and writing content so that generative AI search engines (such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews) can retrieve it, extract a clear passage and cite the page in the answer they generate. Google’s AI features draw on pages Google can crawl and index, and AI Mode breaks a question into several related searches, a technique Google calls query fan-out. Pages that clearly answer those related questions, with evidence, give Google more to use. What kind of content gets cited most? Vague, promotional copy gives an AI engine nothing reliable to quote. Do you use AI to write GEO content? We use AI for research and drafting support. copy_text: Home Services SEO Content Systems [ Services / SEO Content ] SEO content writing services. Content that ranks, gets cited and converts. It is the process behind the writing. Six stages, run the same way for every page, so quality doesn't depend on who happened to write it. 01 · Research Search & audience What your buyers search for at each stage, what already ranks, and what your competitors miss. 02 · Map Topic map Pillar and cluster pages planned around your services, so each page has one job and none compete. 03 · Brief Briefs with expert input Search intent, structure, questions to answer and the expertise we need from your team. 04 · Write Human-written, edited Drafted by writers, checked by editors, fact-checked and reviewed by your experts. 05 · Publish Published & linked Titles, structure, schema and internal links set, and the page linked into its cluster. 06 · Refresh Measured & updated Performance reviewed, then pages refreshed, merged or retired on a schedule. [ Why programmes stall ] Why do most content programmes stall? Not for lack of a strategy. The Content Marketing Institute's 2026 survey of 1,015 B2B marketers shows where it breaks. 40% Content that converts name creating content that prompts action (such as a conversion) as a top challenge. 39% Not enough resource cite constraints on time, people or budget. 33% Hard to measure struggle to measure how effective their content is. 89% AI is everywhere of AI users use it to generate or optimise written content. 12% …and not always better of those using AI for content say its quality has decreased. 37% Experts left out say fewer than 5% of their in-house experts contribute to thought leadership. Source: Content Marketing Institute, B2B Content and Marketing Trends: Insights for 2026 (October 2025) [ AI & Google ] Does Google penalise AI-written content? No. Google judges quality, not how content was made. But it does act on content produced at scale to game rankings. Here is what Google actually says. Myth "Google bans AI content." Google says "Appropriate use of AI or automation is not against our guidelines." Using it mainly to manipulate rankings is. Source → Myth "AI content gets a ranking boost." Google says "Using AI doesn't give content any special gains. It's just content." Source → Myth "Publish hundreds of pages and some will rank." Google says Many pages made mainly to manipulate rankings, not help users, is scaled content abuse, "no matter how it's created". Source → Myth "Longer articles always rank better." Google says There's no magical word count target: content length alone doesn't matter for ranking. Source → Myth "Authorship doesn't matter." Google says Consider accurate author bylines wherever readers might ask "Who wrote this?", and disclose AI use where they'd ask "How was this created?" Source → Our policy: AI helps with research, outlines, transcripts and checks. People write, edit and fact-check every page, and your experts approve it. [ What we write ] What content do we produce? SEO content writing, website copywriting and blog writing, all planned inside one system. 01 · Services Service & solution pages The pages that sell: clear, specific and built to rank for buying-stage searches. 02 · Pillars Pillar & cluster pages In-depth hub pages and the supporting pages that build topical authority around them. 03 · Blog SEO blog articles Articles that answer real questions your buyers ask, linked to the pages that convert. 04 · Copy Website copywriting Home, about and landing-page copy that is clear to people and to search engines. 05 · Compare Comparison pages Honest comparisons and alternatives pages for buyers weighing their options. 06 · Proof Case studies Real projects and results, written up with your clients' approval. 07 · Guides Guides & resources Useful, citable resources that earn links and mentions over time. 08 · Answers Answer-ready content Clear definitions, FAQs and facts that AI search tools can quote accurately. 09 · Refresh Content refreshes Existing pages updated, merged or retired, often the fastest win. [ Process ] How does an SEO content engagement run? Audit what you have, plan what's missing, then publish steadily, never in bulk. 01 Audit Every existing page: what ranks, what converts, what overlaps and what's out of date. 02 Plan Topic map, priorities and a publishing calendar tied to your services. 03 Interview Your experts, sales and customer teams: the knowledge no competitor has. 04 Produce Brief, write, edit, fact-check, approve and publish, page by page. 05 Refresh Measure every page and update, merge or retire on a schedule. [ Deliverables ] What you get. Content audit : every page rated keep, improve, merge or retire. Topic map : pillars, clusters and the searches each page targets. Editorial calendar : agreed priorities and publishing dates. Briefs : intent, structure, questions and expert input for each page. Written & edited pages : fact-checked and approved by your experts. On-page setup : titles, headings, schema and internal links. Style & AI guidelines : how your content is written and how AI may be used. Monthly report : rankings, traffic, conversions and AI citations per page. [ Measurement ] How do we measure content? Page by page, against what it was written to do. Indexed & ranking Whether each page is indexed and where it ranks for its target searches. Organic traffic Visits from search to each page and cluster. Conversions Enquiries, sign-ups and assisted conversions from content. Engagement Whether readers stay, scroll and click through to the next step. Links & citations Links earned and mentions in AI answers. Content health Pages refreshed, merged or retired, and what that changed. [ Straight answer ] More content is not a strategy. Anyone can publish a hundred articles a month now. Most of them won't rank, won't be cited and won't sell, and publishing at that scale mainly to rank is exactly what Google's scaled-content policy targets. We would rather publish fewer pages that each answer a real question with real expertise, and keep them up to date. [ Who it's for ] Who are SEO content systems for? Content ranks when the site is sound and the brand is trusted. These services cover the rest. Together they form an AI Growth System . SEO content writing is creating web pages, articles and copy that answer what people search for, in a way search engines can understand and trust. Good SEO content is written for people first: it matches the searcher’s intent, shows real expertise, is easy to read, and links to related pages on your site. What is an SEO content system? An SEO content system is the repeatable process behind the writing: research, a topic map, briefs, expert input, drafting, editing, publishing, internal linking and scheduled refreshes. It replaces one-off articles with a programme where every page has a purpose, an owner and a place in a topic cluster. Do you use AI to write content? We use AI where it helps: organising research, outlining, transcribing expert interviews and checking drafts. Every page is written and edited by people, fact-checked, and approved by you or your experts. Google says appropriate use of AI is not against its guidelines, but using AI gives content no special gains: quality is what counts. Who writes the content, and how do you get our expertise? Our writers do the writing; your experts supply what only they know. We interview your specialists, sales and customer teams, turn their knowledge into briefs and drafts, and send pages back for technical review, so the expertise on the page is yours. How many articles will you publish each month? As many as can be done well, agreed in the plan, not promised as a volume target. We publish steadily rather than in bulk, because Google treats many pages made mainly to rank as scaled content abuse, however they are produced. Do you update existing content? Yes. Refreshing, merging or removing outdated pages is part of every programme. Google’s starter guide recommends checking older content and updating it, or deleting it if it is no longer relevant. Everything between a lead arriving and a salesperson calling, plus the campaigns that keep customers engaged. 01 · Capture Forms & lead capture Forms, consent and routing that put every lead in the right place with the right permissions. 02 · Nurture Email nurture journeys Sequences triggered by behaviour (downloads, visits, clicks) that answer the next question a buyer has. 03 · Score Lead scoring A scoring model agreed with sales, so "ready to talk" means the same thing to both teams. 04 · CRM CRM workflows & data Lifecycle stages, field rules, deduplication and syncs that keep your CRM trustworthy. 05 · Handoff Sales alerts & handoff Instant alerts and tasks when a lead is ready, with the context sales needs. 06 · Campaigns Email marketing Newsletters and campaigns planned, written, designed, tested and sent. 07 · Social Social publishing workflows Scheduling, approval and reporting for social posts, so publishing runs on a system. 08 · Delivery Deliverability SPF, DKIM and DMARC, list hygiene and spam-rate monitoring, so your email reaches the inbox. 09 · Report Reporting & attribution Which journeys and campaigns create qualified leads, pipeline and revenue. [ Email rules ] What rules does your marketing email have to follow? Since February 2024, Gmail has enforced sender requirements, and privacy law has always applied. Five things we still hear, and what the rules actually say. Myth "Email authentication is only for big senders." Gmail says All senders must set up SPF or DKIM. Senders of more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail accounts need SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Source → Myth "Hide the unsubscribe link to keep the list big." Gmail says Bulk senders' marketing messages must support one-click unsubscribe and show a clearly visible unsubscribe link, and keep spam rates below 0.3%. Source → Myth "B2B email is exempt from spam law." FTC says CAN-SPAM "makes no exception for business-to-business email". Opt-outs must be honoured within 10 business days. Source → Myth "Buy a list and start emailing." ICO says In the UK you must not email individuals without specific consent. The "soft opt-in" covers your own previous customers, not bought-in lists. Source → Myth "Our agency sends it, so compliance is their problem." FTC says Even if you hire another company to handle your email marketing, "you can't contract away your legal responsibility to comply with the law." Source → Sources: Google, Email sender guidelines · US FTC, CAN-SPAM Act compliance guide · UK ICO, Electronic mail marketing . Not legal advice. [ Process ] How does a marketing automation project run? Clean data and agreed definitions first. Automation only amplifies what it's given. 01 Audit Your CRM, email platform, data quality, deliverability and current journeys. 02 Map Buyer journeys, lifecycle stages and a lead-scoring model agreed with sales. 03 Build Workflows, emails, forms and CRM rules: highest-value journeys first. 04 Test Every branch, email and sync checked before anything goes live. 05 Optimise Monthly review of what creates pipeline, then the next journey. [ Deliverables ] What you get. Automation audit : platform, CRM, data, deliverability and journeys. Journey map : lifecycle stages and the messages for each one. Lead-scoring model : agreed with sales, documented and synced. Workflows built : nurture, handoff, re-engagement and customer journeys. Emails : written, designed and tested across devices. Deliverability setup : SPF, DKIM, DMARC and one-click unsubscribe checked. Documentation : how every workflow works, so your team owns it. Monthly report : clicks, conversions, qualified leads and pipeline. [ Measurement ] How do we measure marketing automation? Not by open rates. Apple's Mail Privacy Protection hides whether an email was really opened. Litmus reported it accounted for 55% of all opens as of March 2024. Clicks & replies Real signs that a person read and acted on the email. Conversions Demo requests, downloads and sign-ups from each journey. Qualified leads Leads that reach the agreed score and are accepted by sales. Speed to lead Time from a lead being ready to sales making contact. Pipeline & revenue Deals and revenue influenced by automated journeys. List health Deliverability, spam complaints, bounces and unsubscribes. Source: Litmus, How to measure email marketing success beyond open rate (June 2024) [ Straight answer ] Automation makes bad follow-up faster. If your data is messy, your message unclear or sales and marketing disagree on what a good lead is, automation will simply do the wrong thing at scale. That's why we fix the data and agree the definitions before we build anything, and why we start with the two or three journeys that matter most, not fifty workflows nobody maintains. Automation turns leads into pipeline. These services bring the leads in and extend automation across the business. Together they form an AI Growth System . Leads Lead Generation Systems The campaigns, pages and offers that bring qualified leads in. Explore → Operations AI Workflow Automation AI-powered workflows beyond marketing: operations, sales and service. Explore → Content SEO Content Systems The guides and case studies your nurture journeys send. Explore → Search Search Engine Optimization Organic visibility that brings buyers to your forms in the first place. Explore → System Search Authority OS Search, content and automation run as one operating system. Explore → [ Questions ] About marketing automation. What is marketing automation? Marketing automation is software that sends the right message to each lead at the right time based on what they do: filling in a form, clicking an email, visiting a pricing page. It runs nurture emails, scores leads, updates your CRM and alerts sales when a lead is ready, so no enquiry is forgotten and sales spends time on the leads most likely to buy. Is marketing automation the same as email marketing? No. Email marketing is one channel: newsletters and campaigns. Marketing automation connects email with your website, forms, CRM and sales team, and sends messages triggered by each person’s behaviour. We run both: campaigns for everyone, and automated journeys for each stage of the buying process. Which platform do you use? Usually the one you already have. Most businesses already pay for a CRM and an email platform that can automate far more than they use it for. We audit what you have, recommend changes only where they are needed, and build on it, so you keep ownership of your data and workflows. Is our email compliant? We check. Gmail requires every sender to authenticate with SPF or DKIM, and senders of more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail accounts to use SPF, DKIM and DMARC, offer one-click unsubscribe and keep spam rates below 0.3%. In the US, CAN-SPAM applies to business-to-business email too; in the UK, PECR requires consent before emailing individuals, with a limited exception for existing customers. Why don’t you report open rates? Because they are no longer reliable. Apple’s Mail Privacy Protection hides whether an email was actually opened, and Litmus reported that it accounted for 55% of all opens as of March 2024. copy_text: Home Services AI Workflow Automation [ Services / AI Workflow Automation ] AI workflow automation services. Let AI do the busywork. Keep control. AI workflow automation uses AI models and integrations to handle repetitive work that involves reading, sorting and writing: triaging emails and tickets, extracting data from documents, drafting replies, updating your CRM, with a person approving anything the AI isn't sure about. Reinforce Lab's AI workflow automation services map your processes, build the workflows on the tools you already use, and run them with testing, logging and human checkpoints built in. Get your free diagnostic → Our guardrails AI workflow Capture · process · check · act Emails, tickets, invoices and forms pass through an AI step that classifies, extracts and drafts; confident results go straight to your systems, uncertain ones go to a person for approval, and every step is logged. INPUTS EMAILS TICKETS INVOICES FORMS AI STEP CLASSIFY EXTRACT DRAFT SURE? YES NO YOUR SYSTEMS CRM ERP HELPDESK HUMAN REVIEW APPROVED AUDIT LOG · EVERY STEP RECORDED CAPTURE CAPTURE PROCESS PROCESS CHECK CHECK ACT ACT [ What we automate ] What can AI workflow automation do? The repetitive work between your systems, where people copy, sort, summarise and chase. 01 · Triage Inbox & ticket triage Emails and tickets read, categorised, prioritised and routed to the right person or queue. 02 · Extract Document data extraction Invoices, forms, orders and contracts turned into structured data in your systems. 03 · Draft Drafted replies Responses drafted from your policies and history, sent after review where it matters. 04 · Update CRM & record updates Records created and updated from emails, calls and forms. No more copy and paste. 05 · Enrich Lead enrichment & routing New leads researched, scored and routed to sales with the context they need. 06 · Summarise Reports & summaries Meetings, threads and data summarised into the updates people actually read. 07 · Answer Knowledge assistants Answers drawn from your own documents and policies, with sources shown. 08 · Content Content operations Briefs, first drafts, metadata and checks inside a reviewed content workflow. 09 · Connect System handoffs Work passed between CRM, helpdesk, finance and email without anyone re-keying it. [ Why AI projects stall ] Why do so many AI projects stall at the pilot? Almost everyone uses AI. Few have built it into how work actually flows. McKinsey's 2025 global survey shows the gap. 88% Use AI somewhere of respondents say their organisation regularly uses AI in at least one business function, up from 78% a year earlier. 62% Trying AI agents say their organisation is at least experimenting with AI agents. 39% See profit impact report any impact on EBIT at the enterprise level from AI. The organisations getting the most value are redesigning their workflows instead of adding AI tools on top. That is where we start. Source: McKinsey, The state of AI in 2025: Agents, innovation, and transformation (November 2025) [ Guardrails ] How do we keep AI automation safe? Six controls in every workflow we build. We use the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (govern, map, measure, manage) as our checklist. 01 · People Human in the loop Uncertain or high-stakes cases go to a person before anything happens. 02 · Thresholds Confidence limits Clear rules for what runs automatically, set by you and easy to change. 03 · Logging Audit trail Every input, decision and action recorded, so you can see what happened and why. 04 · Testing Tested on real cases Workflows checked against real examples before launch and monitored after. 05 · Data Minimum data, limited access Only what each step needs is shared, and only the right accounts can see it. 06 · Disclosure Honest with people Anyone talking to an AI assistant is told so, as the EU AI Act requires for chatbots. "When using AI systems such as chatbots, humans should be made aware that they are interacting with a machine so they can take an informed decision." European Commission, AI Act Sources: European Commission, AI Act · NIST, AI Risk Management Framework . Not legal advice. [ Process ] How does an AI automation project run? One workflow at a time, measured against how it works today. 01 Map How the work is done today: steps, systems, volumes, exceptions and time spent. 02 Prioritise The workflows with the most volume, the least risk and the clearest rules first. 03 Pilot One workflow built with human review on every case until it proves itself. 04 Measure Time saved, accuracy and override rate against the baseline. 05 Scale Automation widened where it earns trust, then handed over with documentation. [ Deliverables ] What you get. Process map : how the work flows today and where time goes. Automation roadmap : workflows ranked by value, effort and risk. Built workflows : integrations, AI steps, rules and review queues. Test set : real examples each workflow is checked against. Guardrails : thresholds, logging, access controls and data map. Documentation : how each workflow works and how to change it. Team training : so your people can run and improve it. Monthly report : hours saved, accuracy, overrides and cost per task. [ Measurement ] How do we measure AI automation? Against the baseline we record before anything changes. Hours saved Time no longer spent on the task, measured against the baseline. Turnaround time How quickly requests are handled from arrival to done. Accuracy Share of cases handled correctly, checked against a sample. Override rate How often people change or reject what the AI did. Cost per task Labour saved, minus AI and platform costs. Adoption Whether the team actually uses the workflow, week by week. [ Straight answer ] Not every process should be automated. Some work is rare, high-stakes or depends on judgement that a model can't be trusted with. Automating it creates risk, not savings. We will tell you which processes to leave alone, which to automate fully, and which to automate with a person approving the result, and we measure every workflow against how it worked before. [ Who it's for ] Who is AI workflow automation for? Teams whose people spend hours a week reading, sorting, copying and chasing between systems. 01 Pharmaceutical & Life Sciences Document triage and data extraction with review steps built in Medical-information enquiries routed and drafted for approval Audit trails suited to regulated processes Explore → 02 Healthcare Referral, enquiry and form processing Admin inbox triage that keeps clinicians out of email Patient data minimised and access controlled Explore → 03 B2B SaaS Support ticket triage and drafted replies Lead enrichment and routing into the CRM Customer feedback summarised for product teams Explore → 04 E-commerce Order, return and supplier email handling Product data extracted and cleaned from supplier files Customer-service drafts checked before sending Explore → 05 Manufacturing Quotes, purchase orders and specs extracted from documents Supplier and order updates synced between systems Service reports summarised automatically Explore → 06 Technology IT and service-desk triage Knowledge assistants built on your own documentation Release notes and status updates drafted from tickets Explore → 07 Professional Services Client intake and document review workflows Meeting notes turned into actions in your systems Time-consuming admin handed to AI with partner sign-off Explore → 08 Education Admissions enquiry triage and drafted replies Application documents checked and data extracted Student-service questions answered from your own policies Explore → [ Related services ] What works with AI workflow automation? Automation pays off most when strategy, marketing and sales run on the same system. Together they form an AI Growth System . Strategy Executive AI Consulting Where AI should (and shouldn’t) go in your business, and in what order. Explore → Marketing Marketing Automation Nurture, scoring and sales handoff for every lead. Explore → Sales Lead Generation Systems Channels, landing pages, qualification and routing as one system. Explore → Content SEO Content Systems Content workflows where AI assists and people write, edit and approve. Explore → AI visibility LLM Optimization How AI models describe your business to the people asking about it. Explore → System Search Authority OS Search, content and automation run as one operating system. Explore → [ Questions ] About AI workflow automation. What is AI workflow automation? AI workflow automation uses AI models together with integrations between your systems to handle repetitive work that involves reading, sorting or writing: triaging emails and tickets, extracting data from documents, drafting replies, updating records. A person reviews anything the AI isn’t confident about, and every step is logged. How is it different from ordinary automation? Traditional automation follows fixed rules: if this, then that. It breaks when the input is messy. AI can read unstructured input (an email, a PDF, a free-text form), classify it and extract what matters, so work that used to need a person can flow automatically, with rules and human checks around it. Which tools do you use? Whatever fits your stack. We usually build on the systems you already have (your CRM, helpdesk, email and document storage) connected through an integration platform and an AI model chosen for the task. The choice is made after mapping the process, not before. Is our data safe? We design for it: only the data a step needs is sent to an AI model, access is limited to the accounts that need it, and we document where each piece of data goes. Sensitive processes can be kept inside your own environment or given a human review step. What does “human in the loop” mean? It means the workflow sends uncertain or high-stakes cases to a person before anything happens, for example, a refund above a limit or an email the AI isn’t sure how to answer. Confident, routine cases go straight through. The threshold is yours to set and change. Does the EU AI Act apply to us? It depends on what the AI does. The Act bans a small set of practices (in force since February 2025) and puts strict duties on high-risk uses such as CV sorting in recruitment, due from December 2027. It also requires that people are made aware when they are talking to a chatbot. Most back-office automation is lower risk, but we check each use case. This is not legal advice. How much do AI workflow automation services cost? It depends on how many workflows are in scope, the systems they connect to and how much checking by people each one needs. Automation projects are scoped and priced after the diagnostic, and you get a written scope before the build starts. How long does an AI workflow automation project take? It depends on the process and the systems involved. We start with one workflow where the manual work is highest, test it on real examples with a person approving the output, and extend to further workflows once the first one runs reliably. How do I choose an AI automation agency? Ask how the agency tests its workflows, what happens when the AI is unsure, and where your data goes. A good AI automation agency builds on the tools you already use, keeps a person in the loop for anything uncertain, logs every step, and hands over documentation so you are not locked in. Rarely because nobody knows what to do. Usually because nobody owns the standard, and the site changes faster than anyone checks it. 01 · Templates One mistake, thousands of URLs A faulty pagination, filter or canonical rule in one template repeats on every page built from it, and junk URLs crowd out the pages that matter. 02 · Queues Fixes wait behind features SEO issues sit in engineering backlogs without clear specifications, owners or acceptance criteria, so they don't ship. 03 · Releases Every launch is a risk Redesigns, platform changes and rebrands change URLs, rendering and internal links, often without an SEO check before release. 04 · Teams Many publishers, no rules Content, product, regional and agency teams publish to their own conventions, creating duplicates and pages that compete with each other. 05 · Authority Shortcuts that backfire Pressure for quick links leads to paid placements and exchanges that Google treats as link spam. 06 · Reporting Averages hide the problem Site-wide totals mask the page groups and markets that are falling, so the wrong work gets prioritised. [ What we do ] What does enterprise SEO strategy cover? Nine workstreams under one standard, scoped to what your organisation needs, not sold as a bundle. 01 · Governance SEO standards & ownership Written standards, a clear owner for each rule, and checklists your content, product and engineering teams can follow. 02 · Templates Template-level technical SEO Crawling, indexing, rendering, canonicals, pagination and faceted navigation fixed where they are generated. 03 · Releases Release & QA gates SEO checks before launches and after them, so regressions are caught in staging, not in Search Console. 04 · Migrations Migrations & replatforming URL maps, redirect plans, staged moves and post-launch monitoring for redesigns, mergers and domain changes. 05 · Markets International architecture Country and language structure, hreflang and market launches governed from one standard. 06 · Content Content systems at scale Topic ownership, briefs and editorial QA so many teams publish helpful, non-competing pages. 07 · Authority Digital PR & earned links Newsworthy data, expert commentary and partner relationships that earn links and mentions, never bought. 08 · AI search Visibility in AI answers How AI search tools describe and cite your brand, tracked alongside classic search. 09 · Reporting Forecasts & reporting Baselines by page group and market, forecasts with stated assumptions, and reporting tied to leads and revenue. [ Authority & off-page SEO ] How do we build authority without link spam? Off-page SEO is where enterprise brands take the most avoidable risk. These are the link rules we work to, in Google's own words. "Link spam is the practice of creating links to or from a site primarily for the purpose of manipulating search rankings." Google Search spam policies Myth "Buying links in bulk is the fastest way to rank." Google says Buying or selling links for ranking purposes (for money, goods, services or free products) is listed as link spam, along with automated link programs and excessive link exchanges. Source → Myth "Any paid placement breaks Google's rules." Google says Buying links for advertising and sponsorship is a normal part of the web. It isn't a violation as long as the links are qualified with rel="sponsored" or rel="nofollow". Source → Myth "Keyword links in press releases and guest posts build authority." Google says Links with optimised anchor text in articles, guest posts or press releases distributed on other sites are listed as link spam. Source → Myth "A sitewide footer link on partner sites is free authority." Google says Widely distributed links in the footers or templates of various sites are listed as link spam. Source → Myth "Publish on a big site's subfolder to borrow its rankings." Google says Publishing third-party content on a host mainly to exploit the host's ranking signals is site reputation abuse, enforced since 5 May 2024. Connect Partners & industry Associations, partners, events and suppliers where a link reflects a real relationship. Protect Link audits & qualification Review of your existing links and your outbound paid links, qualified with the right rel attribute. Sources: Google, Spam policies for Google web search · Qualify outbound links [ Migrations ] How do we protect rankings during a migration? Migrations are where large sites lose the most visibility in the least time. The protection is in the preparation. 01 Inventory Every URL that has traffic, links or impressions, from crawls, logs, Search Console and analytics. 02 URL map Each old URL mapped to its closest new equivalent, reviewed and signed off. 03 Redirects Permanent server-side redirects, tested in staging and kept for at least a year. 04 Staged launch Move in steps where possible, changing one thing at a time. 05 Monitor Crawl errors, indexing and rankings watched daily until the new URLs settle. "Expect temporary fluctuation in site ranking during the move." Google Search Central, Site moves with URL changes Source: Google, Site moves and migrations [ Process ] How does an enterprise SEO engagement run? Baseline first, standards second, then shipped work, measured by page group. 01 Discover Crawl, logs, Search Console and analytics, plus interviews with the teams that change the site. 02 Baseline Performance by page group and market, and a roadmap ranked by impact and effort, with owners. 03 Standards SEO standards, release checklists and ticket-ready specifications for your teams. 04 Ship Fixes, content and authority work delivered through your sprints and approval routes. 05 Measure What shipped, what stalled and what it changed, then the next priority. [ Deliverables ] What you get. Enterprise SEO audit : crawl, logs, templates, content and links, by page group. Prioritised roadmap : impact, effort, owner and dependencies for every item. SEO standards : rules for templates, content, internal links, schema and releases. Ticket-ready specifications : with acceptance criteria your developers can build to. Release QA : pre-launch and post-launch checks for every significant change. Migration plan : URL map, redirect rules and monitoring when you move or merge. Authority programme : digital PR and partner links within Google's policies. Reporting : visibility, traffic, leads and revenue by page group and market. [ Measurement ] How do we measure enterprise SEO? By page group and market, not a single site-wide average. Indexed, useful pages Share of important pages indexed, and junk URLs removed from the crawl. Visibility by page group Impressions, clicks and rankings for each template and market. Shipped vs stalled How many SEO tickets shipped, how fast, and what they changed. Release regressions SEO issues caught before launch versus found after. Earned authority Quality links and mentions from relevant, independent sources. Leads & revenue Organic conversions and pipeline, including visibility in AI answers. [ Straight answer ] Enterprise SEO is won in the ticket queue. Most large sites already have audits full of the right recommendations. What they lack is the standard, the owner and the ticket that gets each one shipped, and a check that stops the next release from undoing it. That is where we spend our time. We won't promise rankings, and we won't take shortcuts with links that put a brand at risk. [ Who it's for ] Who is enterprise SEO for? Explore → AI search AI Search Optimization Visibility and accurate recommendations across AI search. Explore → Starting point SEO & AI Search Audit A full review of your Google and AI-search performance with a prioritised fix list. Explore → [ Questions ] About enterprise SEO. What is enterprise SEO? Enterprise SEO is search engine optimization for large, complex organisations: sites with thousands of pages or more, several teams publishing and building, and often several countries or brands. The work shifts from fixing single pages to setting standards for templates, releases, migrations and content, so every page the organisation ships meets them, and to earning authority that a large brand can defend. How is enterprise SEO different from regular SEO? The techniques are the same; the scale and the people are not. One template mistake can repeat across thousands of URLs, fixes have to go through engineering queues, and content, product, development and regional teams all change the site. Enterprise SEO adds governance, ticket-ready specifications, release checks and reporting by page group and market. Do you build links? We build authority the way Google allows: digital PR with newsworthy material, partner and industry relationships, and resources worth citing. We don’t buy links that pass ranking credit, run link exchanges or place keyword links in press releases. Google lists those as link spam. Paid placements are fine for exposure, qualified with rel="sponsored" or rel="nofollow". Will a site migration lose our rankings? Google says to expect temporary fluctuation during a move, and that larger sites can take longer than a few weeks to settle. What protects rankings is the preparation: a complete old-to-new URL map, permanent server-side redirects kept for at least a year, a staged move where possible, and close monitoring afterwards. Does crawl budget matter for our site? It depends on size and how often content changes. Google’s crawl budget guide is aimed at sites with about a million or more pages that change weekly, or 10,000 or more that change daily, and Google calls those rough estimates, not exact thresholds. Below that, index quality usually matters more than crawl budget. How do you work with our in-house teams? Inside your existing process. We write standards and checklists your teams can own, turn fixes into tickets with acceptance criteria, review releases before they ship, and report what shipped, what stalled and what it changed, by page group, market and business outcome. We report by page group, so you can see which releases moved which pages. How do I choose an enterprise SEO agency? Ask how the agency works with engineering, legal and brand teams, because that is where enterprise SEO stalls. A good enterprise SEO agency or company writes requirements your developers can ship, plans migrations before they happen, builds links within Google’s policies, and reports in revenue as well as rankings. copy_text: Home Services Technical SEO [ Services / Technical SEO ] Technical SEO services. Fix what stops search engines and AI crawlers. Technical SEO makes sure search engines and AI crawlers can crawl, render, understand and index the pages that matter, quickly, without errors and without wasting effort on junk URLs. Reinforce Lab's technical SEO services find the root causes, fix them, and re-crawl to prove the fix worked. Get your free diagnostic → What we check Site crawl Crawl → fix → index A crawler maps a website: it finds a broken link, a slow page and an orphan page, each is fixed, and every page becomes crawlable, renderable, indexable and fast. HOME SERVICES BLOG INDUSTRIES /SEO /AUDIT /POST-A /POST-B /PHARMA /SAAS /GUIDE 404 200 OK SLOW FAST ORPHAN LINKED CRAWLING… FIXING ROOT CAUSES… VERIFIED & INDEXED CRAWLABLE CRAWLABLE RENDERABLE RENDERABLE INDEXABLE INDEXABLE FAST FAST [ How search works ] Where can a page get stuck? Google describes Search in three stages (crawling, indexing and serving) and says not every page makes it through each one. For JavaScript sites, rendering sits in between. Technical SEO removes what blocks a page at each stage. Crawl The crawler finds and downloads the page by following links and sitemaps. Breaks when Pages are blocked, orphaned, buried deep or lost in redirect chains. Render The page's code runs so the full content can be read. Breaks when Key content only appears after JavaScript that some crawlers never run. Index The content is analysed and stored, with one version chosen as canonical. Breaks when Duplicates, conflicting canonicals or stray noindex rules get in the way. Serve The page is shown for relevant searches, and used by AI features that draw on the index. Breaks when The page is slow, unstable or unclear about what it is. Sources: Google, How Google Search works · JavaScript SEO basics [ What we check ] What does a technical SEO review cover? Nine areas, checked against how Google documents them, and against what AI crawlers can actually read. 01 · Crawlability Can crawlers reach it? robots.txt, internal links, orphan pages, redirect chains, broken links and crawl traps such as endless pagination or filter URLs. 02 · Indexation Should it be in the index? noindex rules, canonicals, duplicate and thin URLs, and what Search Console reports as crawled or discovered but not indexed. 03 · Rendering Is the content in the HTML? Whether headings, text and links exist in the initial HTML or only appear after JavaScript runs. 04 · Performance Is it fast and stable? Core Web Vitals by template and device: loading, responsiveness and layout stability. 05 · Architecture Is the structure clear? URL patterns, click depth, breadcrumbs and internal links that send authority to the pages that matter. 06 · Sitemaps Do sitemaps help? Clean XML sitemaps that list only canonical, indexable URLs: no redirects, no errors, no junk. 07 · Structured data Does the markup match? Schema that is valid and represents the visible page, as Google's guidelines require. 08 · AI access Can AI crawlers read it? Crawler rules per AI company, server-rendered content, and pages that load without errors for bots. 09 · International Are languages paired? hreflang where you serve several languages or regions: every version listing itself and all the others. [ Core Web Vitals ] What are the Core Web Vitals thresholds? Google's three user-experience metrics, with the "good" thresholds it publishes. We measure them per page template, on mobile and desktop. Metric What it measures "Good" threshold LCP Largest Contentful Paint: how fast the main content loads ≤ 2.5 s INP Interaction to Next Paint: how fast the page responds to clicks and taps ≤ 200 ms CLS Cumulative Layout Shift: how much the layout jumps while loading ≤ 0.1 Measured at the 75th percentile of page loads, on mobile and desktop. INP replaced First Input Delay on 12 March 2024. Sources: web.dev: Web Vitals · INP becomes a Core Web Vital [ Myths vs Google ] Which technical SEO beliefs are wrong? Common assumptions, checked against Google's own documentation. Myth "Blocking a page in robots.txt removes it from Google." Google says robots.txt controls crawling. If a page is blocked, Google can't see its noindex rule. To keep it out of the index, let it be crawled and add noindex. Source → Myth "A canonical tag forces Google to pick that URL." Google says rel=canonical is a strong signal, not a command. Conflicting signals (say, a canonical and a redirect pointing different ways) can make Google choose another URL. Source → Myth "If it's in the sitemap, it will be indexed." Google says A sitemap helps discovery but doesn't guarantee that every URL in it will be crawled or indexed. Source → Myth "Every site needs to worry about crawl budget." Google says Crawl budget mainly matters for very large sites (1 million+ pages), fast-changing sites with 10,000+ pages, or sites with many URLs stuck as "Discovered - currently not indexed". For most, the issue is junk URLs, not budget. Source → Myth "If Google can render our JavaScript, every crawler can." Google says Server-side or pre-rendering "is still a great idea" because "not all bots can run JavaScript". AI companies don't document whether their crawlers render it, and a Vercel study observed several that did not. Source → [ Process ] How does a technical SEO engagement run? We don't stop at a list of problems. Every fix is traced to its cause and verified after release. 01 Crawl & collect Crawl the site, and read Search Console, analytics and (where available) server logs. 02 Find root causes Group symptoms by cause. One template or plugin setting can create hundreds of junk URLs. 03 Prioritise Rank fixes by impact and effort, with the pages that earn traffic protected first. 04 Fix safely Implement with your developers or directly in WordPress, tested on a copy of the site before going live. 05 Verify & monitor Re-crawl after release to prove each fix, then watch indexing and Core Web Vitals for regressions. [ Deliverables ] What you get. Technical audit : every issue, grouped by root cause, with severity and affected URLs. URL inventory : which URLs earn traffic or links and must be protected. Prioritised fix plan : ranked by impact and effort, with clear acceptance criteria. Developer-ready tickets : or the fixes themselves, applied on WordPress. Redirect map : for any URL that has to change, tested before launch. Core Web Vitals plan : per template, on mobile and desktop. Crawler & sitemap setup : robots rules, AI-crawler policy and clean sitemaps. Verification crawl : proof after release that each fix worked. [ Measurement ] How do we measure technical SEO? By whether the right pages get crawled, indexed and served, not by a generic health score. Indexed important pages Share of your valuable pages that are actually in the index. Crawl waste Share of crawled URLs that are junk, duplicates or errors. Core Web Vitals pass rate Templates passing all three thresholds at the 75th percentile. Errors and redirect chains Broken links, 4xx/5xx responses and chained redirects over time. AI-crawler access Whether the crawlers you allow can fetch and read your key pages. Organic landing-page results Traffic and conversions on the pages the fixes were for. [ Protect what works ] We don't break what already ranks. Technical fixes can remove traffic as easily as they add it. Before we change anything, we inventory the URLs that earn traffic and links, map redirects for anything that must move, and test on a copy of the site. Nothing that already ranks changes without your approval, and every release is re-crawled. [ Who it's for ] Who is technical SEO for? gated content and country versions indexed correctly Frequently updated product and pipeline pages kept crawlable, current and free of duplicates Clean HTML and structured data so evidence-heavy pages are read accurately Explore → 02 Healthcare Location and practitioner pages at scale without duplicate or thin URLs Fast, stable pages on mobile for people searching on the go Medical content with visible reviewer and update details, marked up to match Explore → 03 B2B SaaS JavaScript-heavy pages rendered so crawlers see the real content Docs, changelogs and help centres organised without crawl waste Marketing site, app and staging kept separate: staging never indexed Explore → 04 E-commerce Filters and sorting that don’t multiply into endless URLs Variants and out-of-stock or discontinued products handled with the right canonical or redirect Category and product templates that pass Core Web Vitals Explore → 05 Manufacturing Large catalogues and spec sheets, including PDFs, made crawlable and indexable Distributor and regional sites without duplicate content Legacy sites migrated without losing the pages that bring enquiries Explore → 06 Technology Architecture that keeps many products and integrations easy to find JavaScript frameworks checked for what crawlers actually receive Developer docs and API references structured for search and AI answers Explore → 07 Professional Services Service, location and team pages structured so each one can rank Insights and articles kept fast, indexable and linked to the right services Clean sites after mergers and rebrands: old domains redirected correctly Explore → 08 Education Course pages that change every intake kept current and indexable Large archives of news, events and past courses consolidated to cut crawl waste Multi-campus and international versions paired with correct hreflang Explore → [ Related services ] What works with technical SEO? Technical SEO is the foundation. These services build on it. Together they form an AI Growth System . Explore → AI search AI Search Optimization The full program for being visible, accurately described and recommended across AI search. Explore → Global International SEO Multi-country and multi-language search: hreflang, market targeting and localised content. Explore → Scale Enterprise SEO Strategy Search strategy for large sites and multi-team organisations. Explore → Upkeep Website Maintenance Updates, security, backups and performance checks that keep your site healthy. Explore → Always on Search Performance Agent The Search Authority OS agent that reads Search Console and analytics continuously and diagnoses drops. Explore → [ Questions ] About technical SEO. What is technical SEO? Technical SEO is the work that makes sure search engines and AI crawlers can crawl, render, understand and index the pages that matter on a website, quickly, without errors and without wasting effort on junk URLs. It covers crawlability, indexation, site architecture, page speed, structured data and access for crawlers. How is a technical SEO audit different from what you deliver? An audit lists problems. We trace each problem to its root cause (often one template or setting that creates hundreds of symptoms), fix it with your team or directly in WordPress, and then re-crawl the site to verify the fix worked. What are the Core Web Vitals thresholds? Google’s web.dev guidance says a good experience means Largest Contentful Paint within 2.5 seconds, Interaction to Next Paint of 200 milliseconds or less, and Cumulative Layout Shift of 0.1 or less, measured at the 75th percentile of page loads on mobile and desktop. Interaction to Next Paint replaced First Input Delay on 12 March 2024. Does blocking a page in robots.txt remove it from Google? No. Google’s documentation says robots.txt controls crawling, not indexing. If a page is blocked from crawling, Google cannot see a noindex rule on it, so the URL can still appear in results. To keep a page out of the index, it must be crawlable and carry a noindex rule. Do AI crawlers see the same page as Googlebot? Not necessarily. Google renders JavaScript, but its own guidance notes that not all bots can run JavaScript. The major AI companies do not document whether their crawlers render JavaScript, and a Vercel study observed several that did not. The safe approach is to make important content available in the page’s initial HTML. Will technical fixes put our current rankings at risk? Not with our process. We inventory every URL that earns traffic or links before changing anything, map redirects for any URL that must move, test changes on a staging or development copy, and re-crawl after release. Nothing that already ranks is changed without your approval. How much do technical SEO services cost? It depends on the size of the site, the platform, how many templates need fixing and whether we implement the fixes or guide your developers. Every engagement is scoped after the free Search Authority Diagnostic, and you get a written scope and price before work starts. For reference, Search Authority OS packages start from $5,000 setup; the packages page shows the tiers. How long do technical SEO services take to show results? A fix is live as soon as it is tested and released. Search engines then have to re-crawl the pages: Google says some changes take effect in a few hours and others take several months. We re-crawl the site after each release and report which fixes have been picked up. How do I choose a technical SEO agency? Ask how the agency finds root causes, not only symptoms, and who implements the fixes. A good technical SEO agency or consultant shows you the evidence for each problem (crawl data, server logs, Search Console), explains the fix in plain language, protects the URLs that already earn traffic, and re-crawls to prove the fix worked. copy_text: Home Services International SEO [ Services / International SEO ] International SEO services. Reach every market in its own language. International SEO makes sure search engines show the right language and country version of your site to each market, and that every version earns rankings of its own. Reinforce Lab's international SEO services plan the structure, implement hreflang, localize with native review and report market by market, following Google's own guidance. Get your free diagnostic → Site structures Market routing hreflang → right page Four language and market versions of one page are linked to each other with hreflang, and a searcher in each market is served the right version: right language, right market, right page. SEARCH EN · X-DEFAULT / DE /de/ FR-CA /fr-ca/ EN-GB /uk/ HREFLANG · EVERY VERSION LISTS EVERY OTHER RIGHT LANGUAGE · RIGHT MARKET · RIGHT PAGE RIGHT LANGUAGE · RIGHT MARKET · RIGHT PAGE [ Site structure ] Country domains, subdomains or subdirectories? Google lists four ways to structure a multi-regional site. Each has trade-offs; this is how Google describes them. Structure Example Strengths (per Google) Drawbacks (per Google) Country domain example.de Clear geotargeting and easy separation; "a strong signal" of the target country; server location irrelevant Targets one country only; more infrastructure; can be expensive or hard to get Subdomain de.example.com Easy to set up and separate; allows different server locations Users may not recognise the target country from the URL; separate sites to maintain Subdirectory example.com/de/ Lowest maintenance; easy to set up; same hosting Users may not recognise the target country from the URL; single server location URL parameter example.com?loc=de n/a Not recommended by Google; hard to segment Source: Google, Managing multi-regional and multilingual sites . Our default for most B2B sites: subdirectories on one strong domain, unless a legal, brand or market reason points elsewhere. [ hreflang ] How does hreflang work? hreflang tells Google which pages are language or regional versions of each other, so each searcher gets the right one. Small mistakes make Google ignore it. These are the rules. Every version lists every version Each page lists itself and all its alternates. If page X links to page Y, page Y must link back, or the annotations may be ignored. Use valid codes Language in ISO 639-1 (e.g. de ), with an optional region in ISO 3166-1 Alpha 2 (e.g. de-AT ). A region on its own is invalid. Set a fallback x-default is used when no other version matches the user's language or region, often a language selector or global page. Pick one method HTML tags, HTTP headers or the XML sitemap. Large sites usually manage hreflang in sitemaps. Example · HTML head of every version <!-- listed on /, /de/, /fr-ca/ and /uk/ alike --> <link rel="alternate" hreflang=" en "    href="https://example.com/" /> <link rel="alternate" hreflang=" de "    href="https://example.com/de/" /> <link rel="alternate" hreflang=" fr-CA " href="https://example.com/fr-ca/" /> <link rel="alternate" hreflang=" en-GB " href="https://example.com/uk/" /> <link rel="alternate" hreflang=" x-default " href="https://example.com/" /> Source: Google, Tell Google about localized versions of your page [ Myths vs Google ] Which international SEO beliefs are wrong? Common assumptions, checked against Google's own documentation. Myth "The HTML lang attribute tells Google what language a page is in." Google says Google uses the visible content of the page to decide its language. It doesn't use code-level language information such as lang attributes, or the URL. Source → Myth "Redirect visitors to their country version automatically, by IP." Google says Avoid automatic redirects between language versions. Googlebot usually crawls from the USA, so redirects can stop users and search engines from reaching every version. Source → Myth "Just set the target country in Search Console." Google says The International Targeting report is deprecated and country targeting is no longer supported. Google still uses hreflang. Source → Myth "Machine-translate every page; it's the fastest way to scale." Google says Its spam policies list automated transformations, including translating, that add little value as scaled content abuse. Translation needs real localization and review. Source → Myth "Same-language pages for different countries will be penalised as duplicates." Google says For similar same-language pages across regions, pick a preferred version and use rel=canonical and hreflang so the right URL is served. Translated pages are not duplicates. Source → [ What we do ] What does international SEO involve? Nine workstreams, from deciding which markets are worth entering to proving each one pays back. 01 · Markets Market prioritisation Demand, competition and fit per country, so you enter the markets worth entering first. 02 · Structure Architecture decision Country domains, subdomains or subdirectories, chosen and documented with the reasons. 03 · hreflang Implementation & QA Reciprocal annotations, valid codes and x-default, validated across every version. 04 · Research Native keyword research How each market actually searches, not a translation of your English keywords. 05 · Localization Native review Pages adapted for language, culture, units and currency, and reviewed by native speakers. 06 · Authority Local signals Mentions, links and listings that matter in each market, not only at home. 07 · Technical Per-locale technical SEO Sitemaps per locale, canonicals, crawlable language selectors and speed in each region. 08 · Measurement Country-level reporting Search Console and analytics split by market, tied to enquiries and revenue. 09 · AI search AI answers per market What AI tools say about you in each language, observed and reported, not assumed. [ Process ] How does an international SEO engagement run? Market by market, so each launch is proven before the next one starts. 01 Prioritise markets Score countries on demand, competition and readiness, and agree the order. 02 Decide the structure Choose the URL structure and write it down, with a redirect plan if anything moves. 03 Build & hreflang Set up the versions, hreflang and sitemaps, then validate every pair before launch. 04 Localize & publish Research and adapt content per market, with native review before anything goes live. 05 Measure per market Report each market separately, fix what's served wrongly, and roll out the next one. [ Deliverables ] What you get. Market priority model : which countries to enter, in which order, and why. Architecture decision record : the chosen structure, alternatives and trade-offs. hreflang map : every page and its alternates, validated for return links and codes. Native keyword research : per market and language, mapped to pages. Localization briefs : what to adapt beyond the words, for each market. Redirect & migration plan : for any URL that changes, tested before launch. Per-locale sitemaps : clean, canonical and in sync with hreflang. Country dashboards : impressions, clicks, enquiries and revenue by market. [ Measurement ] How do we measure international SEO? Market by market, against the baseline taken before launch. Visibility per market Impressions and clicks in each country's search results. Right version served Share of searchers landing on the version meant for their market. hreflang health Missing return links, invalid codes and orphaned versions over time. Indexed pages per locale Whether each version's important pages are actually in the index. Enquiries & revenue by market What each market brings in: the reason to be there. AI answers per language How AI tools describe and recommend you in each market. [ Straight answer ] Translation isn't localization, and hreflang doesn't steer AI. A translated page that ignores how a market searches, buys and speaks rarely ranks. We research and adapt each market properly, with native review. And while Google documents how it uses hreflang, no AI company documents how its assistant picks a country version, so we don't promise it. We implement what Google documents and check what AI tools actually answer in each market. [ Who it's for ] Who is international SEO for? Companies selling in more than one country or language (or planning to) who need each market to perform on its own. 01 Pharmaceutical & Life Sciences Country-specific product information kept separate where approvals and labels differ HCP and patient content localized with medical and regulatory review in each market hreflang only between pages that are true equivalents Explore → 02 Healthcare Services and locations presented in the languages patients use Medical translations reviewed by native clinical reviewers Local contact details and terms for each country Explore → 03 B2B SaaS Localized landing pages, pricing and currency for each market Docs and help-centre language versions paired correctly Market-specific comparison and alternatives content Explore → 04 E-commerce Country stores with the right currency, shipping and returns Products and variants mapped correctly across locales Filter and sort URLs controlled in every language version Explore → 05 Manufacturing Spec sheets and datasheets in each buyer’s language Distributor and regional sites structured without duplicate content Units, standards and certifications localized for each market Explore → 06 Technology New regions launched market by market, not all at once Developer docs localized where adoption justifies it Product names kept consistent across languages Explore → 07 Professional Services Office and jurisdiction pages that reflect local rules Practice-area content adapted to each market’s business context Partner and expert profiles in the relevant languages Explore → 08 Education Programme pages for international applicants in their language Entry requirements and visa information by country Multi-campus and partner sites paired with correct hreflang Explore → [ Related services ] What works with international SEO? Explore → Local Local SEO Visibility in map results and local searches for every location you serve. Explore → [ Questions ] About international SEO. What is international SEO? International SEO makes sure search engines show the right language and country version of a website to each market, and that each version can rank on its own. It covers site structure, hreflang, localized content and keyword research per market, local authority, and reporting country by country. Should we use country domains, subdomains or subdirectories? Google compares the options: country-code domains send the clearest country signal but cost more to run; subdomains are easy to separate; subdirectories on one domain are the lowest maintenance; URL parameters are not recommended. For most B2B companies we recommend subdirectories on one strong domain, unless a legal, brand or market reason points to country domains. What does hreflang do? hreflang tells Google which pages are language or regional versions of each other, so searchers are shown the right one. Every version must list itself and all the others, using ISO language and region codes, and an x-default version can act as the fallback when no other version matches. Should we redirect visitors to their country version automatically? Google advises against automatically redirecting users to a different language version based on what you think their language is. Googlebot usually crawls from the USA, so automatic redirects can stop it (and users) from reaching every version. A visible language or country selector is the safer choice. Can we use machine translation? As a starting point, yes, but not as the finished page. Google’s spam policies list automated translation that adds little value, produced at scale, as scaled content abuse. We use translation tools for drafts and have native speakers review, adapt and localize every page that matters. Does hreflang control which version ChatGPT or Perplexity shows?
